sentences.text: This genus is known only from isolated dermal denticles, which are small, tooth-like scales embedded in the skin. The crown of each scale is roughly pyramid-shaped.
The name Annulicorona means 'ring crown' and refers to a distinct ring structure at the base of the crown on these dermal denticles.
Fossils of this species have been found at two sites in the Xiaowa Formation in Guizhou, China.
The animal is classified in the class Chondrichthyes and belongs to the parent group Elasmobranchii.
The type species for the genus Annulicorona is Annulicorona pyramidalis.
However, the exact classification remains uncertain because the known fossil remains are very fragmentary.
Annulicorona lived between 237 and 233.6 million years ago during the Carnian age of the Triassic period.
